Numerical benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed neural-operator-based implementation bypasses repeated online solution of the time-varying kernel PDE, achieves a significant acceleration of close to three orders of magnitude compared with conventional numerical kernel solvers, and thus enables real-time stabilization of the system on time-varying spatial domain.
tldr: This paper uses neural operators to learn the backstepping kernel for boundary control of parabolic PDEs on time-varying domains, achieving real-time stabilization.
motivation: Real-time implementation of PDE backstepping control for moving-boundary systems is hindered by the need to repeatedly solve time-varying kernel PDEs.
method: The backstepping design is formulated as an operator mapping the moving-boundary trajectory to the kernel, and a DeepONet is trained to approximate this operator from offline data.
result: The neural-operator-based controller achieves exponential stability on finite time intervals and accelerates computation by nearly three orders of magnitude compared to conventional solvers.
conclusion: The proposed learning-based framework enables real-time stabilization of parabolic equations on time-varying domains, bypassing repeated online kernel PDE solutions.

title: Optimizing The Principal Coefficient Of Elliptic Equations Using $L^p$-regularity, $p < \infty$
authors: Ala' Alalabi, Lorena Bociu, Paul Manns
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study coefficient identification problems for elliptic partial differential equations with total variation regularization and control constraints. Existing related literature relies on continuity and differentiability properties of the control-to-state operator with respect to the [MATH]-norm. While this is sufficient for deriving optimality conditions, it is not well-suited for numerical algorithms, as it neglects the spatial extent of perturbations and leads to a qualitative discrepancy compared to [MATH]-norms with [MATH]. In this work, we address this gap by exploiting [MATH]-regularity results to establish differentiability properties of the control-to-state operator with respect to [MATH]-norms for finite [MATH]. Based on this framework, we derive first- and second-order differentiability results for the reduced objective functional and establish first-order optimality conditions involving a restricted subdifferential characterization of the total variation seminorm and corresponding regularity of the associated multipliers. Building on this, we analyze a nonsmooth trust-region method based on an [MATH]-trust region for [MATH] and prove its convergence to first-order stationary points.
tldr: This paper studies coefficient identification for elliptic PDEs with total variation regularization using Lp-regularity for p<∞.
motivation: Existing methods rely on L∞-norm differentiability, which is not well-suited for numerical algorithms due to neglect of spatial extent of perturbations.
method: The authors exploit Lp-regularity results to establish differentiability of the control-to-state operator in Lp-norms, derive optimality conditions, and analyze a nonsmooth trust-region method.
result: They prove convergence of the trust-region method to first-order stationary points under the Lp framework.
conclusion: The Lp-based approach bridges the gap between theory and numerics for PDE-constrained optimization with total variation regularization.

title: Cross-connections Of The Normed Algebra Of Finite Rank Bounded Operators On A Hilbert Space
authors: P. G. Romeo A. Anju
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17796v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article we examine the cross-connections of the normal category of finite dimensional subspaces of a Hilbert space and it's dual space. Further, we describe the cross-connection semigroup of cones, which is a normed algebra isomrphic to the normed algebra of finite rank bounded operators on a Hilbert space. We also characterize compact operators and their spectrum by the normal cones in the normal category of proper subspaces of a Hilbert space.
tldr: This paper studies cross-connections in the normed algebra of finite rank bounded operators on a Hilbert space, focusing on categorical and algebraic structures rather than quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: To understand the algebraic and categorical structure of finite rank operators and compact operators on Hilbert spaces via cross-connections.
method: Uses category theory and normed algebra to analyze normal cones and cross-connection semigroups.
result: Describes a normed algebra isomorphic to the algebra of finite rank bounded operators and characterizes compact operators via normal cones.
conclusion: The cross-connection approach provides an algebraic framework for studying operator algebras, but has no direct application to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Kalman Structure And Observability For Transport Systems
authors: Yacouba Simpore
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17814v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study observability and controllability for constant-coefficient first-order hyperbolic systems on the real line when only part of the state is observed or controlled. Even when the Kalman rank condition holds, the usual \(L^2(\mathbb R)^N\)-observability estimate may fail because some components are detected only through the dynamics. We show that the Kalman structure determines the appropriate observability estimate. A component that becomes visible after \(k\) algebraic steps is measured at low Fourier frequencies with a weight of order \(|\xi|^{2k}\) in the Fourier variable. This yields a natural Kalman-adapted observation space for the system. We also prove localized observability for diagonalizable systems on observation sets with uniformly bounded gaps and, separately, extend the whole-line construction to systems with real spectrum and Jordan blocks.
tldr: This paper studies observability and controllability for constant-coefficient first-order hyperbolic systems on the real line, focusing on the Kalman structure and its effect on observability estimates.
motivation: To understand how partial observation or control affects observability estimates for hyperbolic systems, especially when the Kalman rank condition holds but standard estimates fail.
method: The authors analyze the Kalman structure of the system to derive weighted Fourier estimates for components that become visible after algebraic steps, and prove localized observability for diagonalizable systems.
result: They show that the Kalman structure determines the appropriate observability estimate, with components visible after k steps measured at low Fourier frequencies with weight |ξ|^{2k}, and extend results to systems with real spectrum and Jordan blocks.
conclusion: The Kalman structure provides a natural adapted observation space, and localized observability holds for diagonalizable systems on observation sets with uniformly bounded gaps.

title: On Injectivity Of Phase Retrieval
authors: Zhangsong Li
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17922v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this short note, we prove that if [MATH] with [MATH] has i.i.d.\ standard complex Gaussian entries, then the probability that the phase retrieval map generated by [MATH] is not injective is positive. This proves Part (1) of a conjecture of Cynthia Vinzant, which was later restated by Afonso S. Bandeira in . The main result of this paper was obtained using generative AI, in particular the Rethlas system.
tldr: Proves that phase retrieval maps with i.i.d. standard complex Gaussian matrices are not injective with positive probability.
motivation: To resolve a conjecture about injectivity of phase retrieval maps, which is a problem in signal processing and applied mathematics.
method: Uses probabilistic arguments and properties of Gaussian random matrices to show non-injectivity.
result: Shows that the probability of non-injectivity is positive for such matrices.
conclusion: Part (1) of the conjecture is proven; the result is obtained with the aid of generative AI.

title: A Stone-Cech Collecting Semantics For Residual Process Behaviour
authors: Mike Stannett
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper develops a compact collecting semantics for the residual behaviour left by nonterminating computation. For sequential time this is the tail-cluster set of the stream in the Stone-Cech compactification of the observation space. It gives a common semantics to ordinary recurrence, mixed recurrent behaviour, and escape through noncompact parts of the observation space. The basic theory establishes tail invariance, functoriality under continuous observations, and a temporal reading for clopen observations: containment in the corresponding clopen region of beta-X is eventual truth, while nonempty intersection is recurrence. Progress and fairness assumptions are represented by strengthening the time filter. Relational meanings are obtained by compactifying products, so correlations between observations made along the same asymptotic view of time are retained. The main application is to residual behaviour in CCS. Infinite executions are read as streams of residual processes modulo structural congruence. The resulting semantics distinguishes stable divergence, finite recurrent divergence, mixed recurrence with escape, and escape through unbounded residual growth. It validates residual-tail laws for prefixing, guarded unfolding, finite choice, and finite prefix-choice forms, while also identifying the boundary of those laws under parallel composition and synchronisation. Finite observational quotients provide the computational interface to the compact semantics: abstract meanings become recurrent states and strongly connected component calculations, and resource observations detect unbounded escape without requiring individual points of the Stone-Cech remainder to be inspected.
tldr: Develops a compact semantics for residual process behavior using Stone-Cech compactification, applied to CCS.
motivation: To provide a unified semantic framework for nonterminating computation, including recurrence and divergence.
method: Uses Stone-Cech compactification of observation space to define tail-cluster sets and tail invariance.
result: Distinguishes stable divergence, finite recurrent divergence, mixed recurrence with escape, and unbounded residual growth.
conclusion: The semantics validates residual-tail laws for process algebra constructs and identifies boundaries under parallel composition.

title: Syntactic Systems Cannot See Semantic Invariants
authors: Fabio F. G. Buono
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17275v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We start from a small open question, where Hetzl and Vierling asked whether two theories of induction, open induction and clause set cycles, are incomparable. They proved one direction and left the other open. Here we close it, and the proof is almost embarrassingly short, because the rules for addition can only fire when the first argument is [MATH] or a successor, a Skolem constant is neither, so the terms [MATH] and [MATH] can never be touched, and a machine that can never touch them can never prove they are equal. The thing that separates the two theories is the order of two constants, and that order is a fact about numbers, not about symbols. We extract from this proof a small general principle, the Syntactic Invariance Principle, that names the shape of such arguments. We then close with a few speculative remarks on how this same shape appears, informally, in the known barriers to settling [MATH] versus [MATH], where each barrier seems to point to a level of description that the techniques in the barrier cannot reach. We raise this as a suggestion rather than a theorem, since the analogy is real but we do not push it past the point where we can defend it. Along the way we raise an open question that the analogy suggests but does not settle, on whether a fast algorithm for [MATH], were it to exist, would always be exhibitable as a machine you can write down or whether it could be found, in some cases, only as a function on the numbers.
tldr: The paper discusses a syntactic invariance principle in proof theory and its speculative analogy to barriers in complexity theory, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid systems.
motivation: To resolve an open question about the incomparability of two induction theories and to extract a general principle about syntactic versus semantic reasoning.
method: The author provides a short proof that clause set cycles cannot prove the equality of two Skolem constants, then generalizes this to the Syntactic Invariance Principle, and draws informal analogies to P vs NP barriers.
result: The open question is closed with a simple proof, and a principle is formulated that highlights limitations of syntactic systems in capturing semantic invariants.
conclusion: The syntactic invariance principle may offer a new perspective on known barriers in complexity theory, but this remains speculative.

title: Sa-ra-jscc: SNR-Adaptive And Semantic-Rate-Aware Joint Source-Channel Coding
authors: Shitong Zhang, Yaping Sun, Hao Chen, Xiaoyi Li, Bo Gu, Xiaodong Xu, Nan Ma
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17940v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In joint source-channel coding (JSCC)-based semantic communication systems, achieving stable and reliable image semantic transmission under channel constraints remains a key challenge. In most channel adaptation modules, the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) is often injected into each layer of a channel-adaptation model in an independent and layer-wise manner, which undermines global coordination across layers. Therefore, consistent noise-robust representations may fail to be learned throughout the model. To address this problem, we propose SA-RA-JSCC, a novel channel-adaptive JSCC model. SA-RA-JSCC maps SNR into a unified semantic vector in the feature space and then applies a one-shot global reweighting to the encoded features, thereby enabling globally consistent and learnable channel adaptation. Moreover, in order to further enhance the anti-channel capability of semantic information, a semantic-rate-aware module is introduced, enabling the adaptive policy to respond simultaneously to fluctuations in channel quality and changes in semantic-rate constraints, thereby enhancing global network coordination and channel adaptivity. Extensive experiment results across multiple channels and datasets demonstrate that SA-RA-JSCC significantly outperforms existing semantic communication models in terms of reconstruction metrics such as PSNR and MS-SSIM, exhibiting stronger robustness across a broad range of SNR regimes.
tldr: A joint source-channel coding scheme for semantic communication that adapts to SNR and semantic rate.
motivation: Existing JSCC models lack global coordination across layers when adapting to channel SNR, leading to suboptimal noise-robust representations.
method: Proposes SA-RA-JSCC which maps SNR into a unified semantic vector for global reweighting of encoded features, and adds a semantic-rate-aware module for joint adaptation.
result: Outperforms existing semantic communication models in PSNR and MS-SSIM across various channels and SNR regimes.
conclusion: The proposed method achieves more robust and adaptive image transmission under channel constraints.

title: An Empirical Analysis Of Ai Slop In Music Streaming
authors: Stanley Wu, Josephine Passananti, Viresh Mittal, Wenxin Ding, Haitao Zheng, Ben Y. Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18052v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative AI models lower the bar for content creation, making it easy for any user to create professional-looking images, text and music with minimal effort. This has enabled a new cottage industry around creation of "AI slop" mass quantities of mediocre content produced to generate revenue, often through misrepresentation as human-authored content, or scams involving automated scripts and fake consumption. While there are obvious parallels between the AI-slop industry and "traditional" email spam networks, it might be too early to determine if AI slop generation can grow into a similar self-sustaining industry. In this paper, we look specifically at the music industry, and explore the question: Can we prevent AI music slop from growing into a self-sustaining shadow industry? To answer this question, we characterize the current state of AI slop in music, and its pipeline from generation, distribution, and consumption by users on streaming platforms. By examining growth and engagement on Spotify, we confirm that AI music exhibits AI slop characteristics: the overwhelming majority (93%) of AI music receive few, if any listener plays, and are rarely recommended. AI musicians "spray and pray," releasing large volumes of music across multiple genres in hopes of generating a hit. We also explore the AI slop pipeline by generating and publishing our own AI tracks onto streaming through 11 indie music distributors. We find distributors have inconsistent and largely unenforced policies on AI music, making it surprisingly easy to publish mass produced AI songs. Finally, we consider AI music detection, and find that current methods lack accuracy or robustness. As generation costs decrease, we believe slop generation in music will become self-sustainable, unless concrete steps are taken by the music industry. We consider and discuss potential mitigation methods based on our findings.
tldr: This paper analyzes the phenomenon of AI-generated music slop on streaming platforms, its distribution, and potential mitigation strategies.
motivation: To determine whether AI music slop can become a self-sustaining industry and to characterize its current state.
method: The authors analyze Spotify data, publish their own AI-generated tracks through distributors, and evaluate AI music detection methods.
result: 93% of AI music receives few plays, distributors have inconsistent policies, and current detection methods are inaccurate.
conclusion: Without industry action, AI slop in music will become self-sustaining as generation costs decrease.

title: Learning Red Agent Policy From Observations For Neurosymbolic Autonomous Cyber Agents
authors: Ankita Samaddar, Sandeep Neema, Daniel Balasubramanian, Xenofon Koutsoukos
abstract: ArXiv:2606.18223v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With sophisticated cyber-attacks becoming increasingly prevalent, modern networks require intelligent autonomous cyber-defense agents trained via Reinforcement Learning (RL). These agents employ neurosymbolic approaches such as behavior trees with learning-enabled components (LECs) to learn, reason, adapt, and implement security rules while maintaining critical operations. However, these autonomous networks are partially observable systems, i.e., the cyber-attacker's (red agent's) actions are not observable, making it difficult for the defender to predict red actions, learn red policies, or assess the attacker's intrusion levels. To address this, we propose a Policy Learning Technique using imitation learning to learn policies for partially observable RL agents with discrete states and discrete actions. We apply this technique in an autonomous cyber environment to predict red agent's actions from network observations and defender actions. Integrated with a neurosymbolic cyber-defense agent, our method effectively handles different red policies and achieves high prediction accuracy across diverse simulated scenarios.
tldr: This paper uses imitation learning to predict attacker actions in autonomous cyber defense, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: Autonomous cyber-defense agents need to predict attacker actions in partially observable environments to improve security.
method: The authors propose a policy learning technique based on imitation learning to infer the red agent's policy from network observations and defender actions.
result: The method achieves high prediction accuracy across diverse simulated cyber scenarios.
conclusion: Imitation learning can effectively predict attacker policies in autonomous cyber environments, enhancing neurosymbolic defense agents.

title: The Competitiveness Of Renewables: An Analysis Of Magnitude, Geography, And Drivers
authors: Pascal Fr\"ohlich, Maximilian Bernecker, Felix M\"usgens
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17063v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While renewable energy sources are the fastest-growing electricity generation technology globally, their competitiveness is still the subject of controversy. This paper presents an electricity system model for investment and dispatch to determine the cost-optimal shares of renewable energy sources. We compute and analyse renewable generation shares in market equilibrium for Germany and Texas, using annual data for 2015 to 2024, and in five-year intervals for 2030 to 2050. Furthermore, we identify the key drivers of the renewable competitiveness and quantify their contribution through parameter variations. Our results show that renewable generation achieves considerable market shares even without subsidies. In Germany, the increase in renewable generation is primarily driven by CO2 pricing, complemented by declining investment costs for renewable technologies. In Texas, solar PV is part of the cost-optimal system, even in the absence of CO2 pricing and despite low natural gas prices.
tldr: This paper analyzes the competitiveness of renewable energy sources in Germany and Texas using an electricity system model.
motivation: To determine cost-optimal shares of renewables and identify key drivers of their competitiveness.
method: An electricity system model for investment and dispatch is used with annual data from 2015-2024 and projections to 2050.
result: Renewables achieve considerable market shares even without subsidies; CO2 pricing and declining investment costs are key drivers.
conclusion: Renewable energy is competitive under current and projected conditions, with solar PV viable even without CO2 pricing in Texas.

title: Mass Extinctions By Gravitational Tides
authors: Daniele Fargion
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17105v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Past and recent observations suggest that many planetary mass or dwarf planet objects may exist in the outer Solar System. Gravitational perturbations may occasionally bring some of them into the inner Solar System. The early, rare collision between the early Earth and a Mars sized body is generally invoked to explain the formation of the Moon. More probable than a direct impact, are grazing or near Earth flybys of similar objects. Such passages may have left strong tidal signatures: giant waves, large volcanic episodes, sea regressions, coherent meteor showers, and major climatic perturbations. These mechanisms could have contributed to several major biological mass extinctions over the past [MATH] million years, as suggested by peculiar correlations in the geological record. Similar events may have occurred several times during the earlier history of Earth. Accretion of mini planets by largest planets and in particular by the Sun may also have occurred many more times over the last four billion years. Possibly producing additional temperature variations on planets and Earth.
tldr: The paper proposes that gravitational tides from flybys of planetary-mass objects in the outer Solar System may have caused mass extinctions on Earth.
motivation: To explain biological mass extinctions and geological events through gravitational perturbations rather than direct impacts.
method: The author correlates geological records with hypothetical scenarios of near-Earth flybys by dwarf planets or planetary bodies, analyzing tidal effects.
result: The paper suggests that such flybys could produce giant waves, volcanic activity, sea regressions, and climatic changes linked to extinction events.
conclusion: Gravitational tides from outer Solar System objects may have contributed to several major mass extinctions over the past 500 million years.

title: Public Transit Gains And Spatially Uneven Travel Demand Changes After Nyc Congestion Pricing
authors: Donghang Li, Dingyi Zhuang, Yunlin Li, Chenan Shen, Nina Cao, Yunhan Zheng, Shenhao Wang, Jinhua Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17530v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: New York City implemented the nation's first cordon-based congestion pricing program in January 2025, providing an opportunity to evaluate how system-wide urban mobility responds to large-scale pricing interventions. Because such policies generate spillovers across modes and locations, credible control groups are difficult to construct. We address this challenge using time series foundation models to generate probabilistic counterfactual demand forecasts with calibrated uncertainty. Applying this framework to bus, subway, and aggregate trip volume data, we find that post-policy bus and subway ridership increased significantly relative to expected no-policy demand, while overall travel demand decreased modestly. The effects are spatially heterogeneous: while reductions in overall travel demand are concentrated within the Congestion Relief Zone, transit gains extend beyond Manhattan's core. Socio-demographic analyses further reveal uneven adaptation across neighborhoods, highlighting spatial equity implications. Our framework provides a scalable approach for the uncertainty-aware evaluation of system-wide urban interventions when clean control groups are unavailable.
tldr: This paper evaluates the impact of NYC's congestion pricing on public transit ridership and travel demand using time series foundation models.
motivation: To assess how a large-scale pricing intervention affects urban mobility and to address the challenge of constructing credible control groups.
method: Time series foundation models generate probabilistic counterfactual demand forecasts with calibrated uncertainty, applied to bus, subway, and aggregate trip volume data.
result: Post-policy bus and subway ridership increased significantly relative to expected no-policy demand, while overall travel demand decreased modestly, with spatially heterogeneous effects.
conclusion: The framework provides a scalable approach for uncertainty-aware evaluation of urban interventions, highlighting spatial equity implications.

title: Constitutive Modelling Of Magneto-active Polymers At Finite Strains: A Survey
authors: Abhishek Ghosh, Chennakesava Kadapa, Mokarram Hossain
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magneto-active polymers (MAPs) are field-responsive soft composites whose mechanical behaviour can be actively modified by external magnetic fields. Their ability to exhibit field-induced stiffening, magnetostriction, anisotropy and rate-dependent response makes them attractive for sensors, actuators, adaptive structures, vibration-control devices and soft robotic systems. This article presents a structured survey of constitutive modelling approaches for MAPs at finite strains. The review traces the development from early semi-empirical descriptions to thermodynamically consistent nonlinear continuum theories, with particular attention to isotropic and anisotropic magnetoelastic constitutive models, invariant-based and spectral representations, variational and polyconvex frameworks, microstructurally motivated models, dispersed-chain descriptions and magneto-viscoelastic theories. The principal constitutive variables, energy functions, coupling mechanisms and physical assumptions underlying the main models are discussed. The survey shows that constitutive modelling of MAPs has developed into a broad family of nonlinear, anisotropic and dissipative frameworks capable of describing versatile behaviours observed experimentally. Important challenges remain in resolving thermo-magneto-mechanical coupling and microstructure-sensitive effects, identification of parameters, validation of models as well as robust and efficient implementation on computers.
tldr: A survey of constitutive models for magneto-active polymers at finite strains.
motivation: To provide a structured overview of modeling approaches for MAPs, which are used in sensors, actuators, and soft robotics.
method: Review of literature covering isotropic/anisotropic magnetoelastic models, invariant-based frameworks, variational principles, and microstructurally motivated theories.
result: Identifies a broad family of nonlinear, anisotropic, dissipative models, but notes unresolved challenges in thermo-magneto-mechanical coupling and parameter identification.
conclusion: Constitutive modeling of MAPs has matured but still requires further development in coupling effects and computational implementation.

title: Latent Residual-Closure Fourier Neural Operator For Robust Multi-Field Solving In Particle-in-Cell Simulations
authors: Linlin Zhong Jianhua Lyu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17733v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations are widely used for kinetic plasma modeling in energy applications, but their efficiency is often limited by repeated field solves on dense meshes. This work proposes a Latent Residual-Closure Fourier Neural Operator (LRC-FNO) for robust surrogate multi-field solving in PIC simulations. Rather than treating field prediction as a purely data-driven regression task, LRC-FNO formulates PIC field solving as a two-level residual-closure problem involving source compression and source-to-field operator mapping. An autoencoder extracts compact representations of particle-deposited source fields, while a Latent Closure Refiner recovers unresolved residual structures lost during compression. A Coarse-FNO Solver captures the dominant field response, and a Residual-Closure FNO restores full-resolution corrections. The method is tested on three benchmarks with increasing complexity: 1D linear Landau damping (LLD), 2D two-stream instability (TSI), and a 2D scrape-off layer (SOL) fusion plasma model. In LLD and TSI, LRC-FNO better preserves charge-to-potential mapping, potential-mode evolution, residual charge structures, and particle-field energy exchange during closed-loop PIC integration. In the SOL case, LRC-FNO achieves relative L2 errors of 0.0447 for the self-consistent potential and 0.0251 for the magnetic vector potential in single-step prediction. More importantly, when used as a neural initial guess with 20 iterative corrections, LRC-FNO maintains strong physical consistency in extrapolated closed-loop simulations, preserving charge and current density structures over a time range close to twice the training horizon. These results demonstrate that LRC-FNO can serve as both a fast surrogate field solver and a high-quality initialization strategy for iterative PIC field solvers.
tldr: This paper proposes a neural operator (LRC-FNO) for accelerating field solves in particle-in-cell plasma simulations, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: PIC simulations are computationally expensive due to repeated field solves on dense meshes; the authors aim to develop a fast surrogate solver.
method: LRC-FNO uses an autoencoder for source compression, a latent closure refiner to recover residuals, a coarse FNO solver for dominant field response, and a residual-closure FNO for full-resolution corrections.
result: The method achieves low relative L2 errors on benchmarks (e.g., 0.0447 for potential in SOL case) and maintains physical consistency in extrapolated simulations up to twice the training horizon.
conclusion: LRC-FNO can serve as both a fast surrogate field solver and a high-quality initialization for iterative PIC solvers.

title: Moment Generating Function Of The Tacnode Process
authors: Taiyang Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17771v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The tacnode process is a universal determinantal point process arising in non-intersecting particle systems and random tiling models. In this paper, we study the generating function for the counting functions of the tacnode process on a union of [MATH] intervals, [MATH]. Our first result provides an integral representation for the [MATH]-point generating function in terms of the Hamiltonian governing a system of [MATH] coupled differential equations. Combined with several differential identities for this Hamiltonian, the representation yields the large gap asymptotics, up to and including the constant term. As further applications, we obtain asymptotic formulae for the expectations, variances, and covariances of the counting functions, and establish a central limit theorem for their joint fluctuations. These results extend the previously known [MATH]-point theory for the tacnode process to the multi-interval setting with multiple discontinuities.
tldr: The paper studies the tacnode process, a determinantal point process from random matrix theory, deriving generating functions and large gap asymptotics.
motivation: To understand the multi-interval statistics of the tacnode process, which arises in non-intersecting particle systems and random tilings.
method: Uses integrable operator theory and Hamiltonian systems to derive integral representations for the generating function, then applies differential identities for asymptotic analysis.
result: Obtains large gap asymptotics including constant term, and asymptotic formulas for expectations, variances, covariances, and a central limit theorem for joint fluctuations.
conclusion: Extends the known one-point theory of the tacnode process to multi-interval settings with multiple discontinuities.

title: When Volumetric Growth Selects Surface Growth
authors: Rohn Abeyaratne, Roberto Paroni, Marco Picchi Scardaoni
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17774v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the relationship between volumetric and surface growth within a recently proposed optimization-driven framework for linearly elastic solids. In this approach, growth is not prescribed through an evolution law; instead, the growth distribution is determined as the solution of a constrained optimization problem. Focusing on processes driven by the minimization of the work performed by external loads in one-dimensional and axisymmetric settings, we derive explicit analytical solutions for the resulting growth distributions. Although growth is initially formulated as a volumetric process through a distributed growth strain tensor, we show that the optimal growth distributions are singular and concentrate on boundaries or internal interfaces. These results provide a variational mechanism through which, under certain conditions, surface growth is selected as the optimal realization of volumetric growth.
tldr: This paper studies volumetric vs. surface growth in elastic solids using optimization, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To understand why surface growth often dominates over volumetric growth in biological and physical systems.
method: Formulates growth as a constrained optimization problem minimizing external work, solved analytically in 1D and axisymmetric settings.
result: Optimal growth distributions are singular and concentrate on boundaries or interfaces, showing surface growth emerges naturally from volumetric growth optimization.
conclusion: Surface growth can be understood as a variational consequence of volumetric growth under certain conditions.

title: On The Strong Duality In Continuous-time And Discrete-time Linear Quadratic Regulators
authors: Yang Zheng Yuto Watanabe
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17208v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper revisits the strong duality in the linear quadratic regulator (LQR) for continuous-time and discrete-time systems, and explores its interconnection with typical assumptions and the uniqueness of primal-dual solutions. Using a linear operator [MATH], we formulate a common nonconvex LQR problem that captures both time domains. We then derive its Lagrange dual problem and establish the strong duality via a rank-constrained tight semidefinite program (SDP) relaxation. Further, we show that the primal-dual optimal solutions to the SDP relaxation, after dropping the rank constraint, recover the classical algebraic Riccati equations and optimal feedback gains in a constructive manner. The dual derivation and strong duality analysis rely on mild standard assumptions and exploit the properties of the linear operator and its adjoint, revealing a structural symmetry between the two time domains.
tldr: This paper studies strong duality in linear quadratic regulators using semidefinite programming relaxations.
motivation: To understand the relationship between primal and dual solutions in LQR problems and recover classical Riccati equations.
method: Formulates a nonconvex LQR problem via a linear operator, derives its Lagrange dual, and establishes strong duality through a rank-constrained SDP relaxation.
result: Primal-dual optimal solutions to the SDP relaxation recover the algebraic Riccati equations and optimal feedback gains.
conclusion: Strong duality holds under mild assumptions, revealing structural symmetry between continuous-time and discrete-time LQR.

title: Strong-Winning Target Avoidance For Manneville--Pomeau Maps
authors: Jason Duvall
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17224v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that target-avoidance sets for Manneville--Pomeau maps are strong winning for Schmidt's game. More precisely, for the class of nonuniformly expanding interval maps considered here, there exists a single parameter [MATH] such that for every target [MATH], the set of points whose forward orbit does not accumulate on [MATH] is [MATH]-strong winning. The proof induces on the uniformly expanding region [MATH]. The resulting first-return map has infinitely many branches, so we approximate it by finite-branch expanding maps, apply a theorem of Hu--Li--Yu to those finite approximants, and then transfer the resulting strategies first to the induced map and then to the original Manneville--Pomeau map.
tldr: This paper proves strong-winning target avoidance for Manneville-Pomeau maps using Schmidt's game.
motivation: To understand the fractal geometry and dynamical properties of nonuniformly expanding maps.
method: Induces on the uniformly expanding region, approximates the first-return map by finite-branch expanding maps, applies a theorem of Hu-Li-Yu, and transfers strategies back.
result: There exists a single parameter such that for every target, the set of points whose forward orbit does not accumulate on the target is strong-winning.
conclusion: The result contributes to the theory of Schmidt's game and dynamical systems, but has no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Adaptive Proximal Methods For Weakly Convex Optimization With Unknown Parameter: Deterministic And Stochastic Guarantees
authors: Miaolan Xie
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17285v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many nonsmooth, nonconvex objectives in learning and signal recovery are [MATH]-weakly convex. We minimize such a function in deterministic and stochastic settings when the weak-convexity parameter [MATH] is unknown. The objective is not required to be globally Lipschitz continuous or smooth. We propose the Adaptive Prox-Guided Scheme (APS), a one-trial proximal algorithm that adapts the proximal parameter online and bidirectionally through a descent test, allowing it to exploit favorable local structure. In the deterministic setting, APS obtains an [MATH] iteration complexity for producing an [MATH]-subgradient stationary point. In the stochastic setting, APS achieves a high-probability [MATH] iteration bound for driving the Moreau-envelope gradient below [MATH]. This result holds under deliberately weak oracle assumptions: the function-difference estimates may be biased and heavy-tailed, and the stochastic proximal oracle need only be sufficiently accurate with constant probability when the proximal parameter lies below [MATH] (unknown to the algorithm), and can be arbitrary otherwise.
tldr: This paper proposes an adaptive proximal method for weakly convex optimization with unknown weak-convexity parameter, providing deterministic and stochastic convergence guarantees.
motivation: Many nonsmooth, nonconvex objectives in learning and signal recovery are weakly convex, but existing methods often require knowledge of the weak-convexity parameter or global Lipschitz continuity.
method: The Adaptive Prox-Guided Scheme (APS) adapts the proximal parameter online via a descent test, requiring only function-difference estimates and a stochastic proximal oracle with minimal accuracy assumptions.
result: In the deterministic setting, APS achieves O(1/ε^2) iteration complexity for an ε-subgradient stationary point; in the stochastic setting, it achieves high-probability O(1/ε^4) iteration bound for driving the Moreau-envelope gradient below ε.
conclusion: APS efficiently solves weakly convex optimization problems without prior knowledge of the weak-convexity parameter, under weak oracle assumptions.

title: Domain Decomposition Methods For The Stokes-Biot Model Of Fluid-poroelastic Structure Interaction
authors: Manraj Ghumman, Manu Jayadharan, Ivan Yotov
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17363v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a non-overlapping domain decomposition method for the numerical solution of the Stokes-Biot model of fluid-poroelastic structure interaction in a mixed form. The model is based on a velocity-pressure formulation for the free fluid, a three-field stress-displacement-rotation formulation with weakly symmetric stress for the solid deformation, and a Darcy velocity-pressure formulation for the fluid in the poroelastic media. Mass conservation, balance of stress, and the Beavers-Joseph-Saffman slip with friction condition are imposed on the interface. The interface conditions are incorporated through Lagrange multipliers modeling the traces of the displacement and the Darcy pressure. The system is discretized using stable mixed finite element spaces for Stokes flow, elasticity, and Darcy flow. The domain is decomposed into a union of subdomains of either Stokes or Biot type with three types of interfaces: Stokes-Stokes, Biot-Biot, and Stokes-Biot. On the Stokes-Stokes interfaces, a normal stress Lagrange multiplier is introduced to impose weakly velocity continuity, while the Biot-Biot and Stokes-Biot interfaces are equipped with displacement and pressure Lagrange multipliers to impose weakly continuity of normal stress and normal velocity, respectively. The global problem is reduced via Schur complement to an interface problem for the Lagrange multipliers, which is solved by GMRES. Each iteration requires the solution of local Stokes or Biot problems, which can be performed in parallel. We show that the resulting interface operator is positive definite and analyze the convergence of the GMRES iteration through fields-of-value analysis. Numerical experiments are presented to illustrate the performance of the method.
tldr: This paper develops domain decomposition methods for the Stokes-Biot model of fluid-poroelastic structure interaction, focusing on numerical analysis and parallel computing.
motivation: Efficient numerical simulation of fluid flow in deformable porous media is important for geophysics and biomechanics, but requires robust domain decomposition techniques.
method: A non-overlapping domain decomposition method is formulated with Lagrange multipliers on interfaces, reduced to an interface problem solved by GMRES, with local Stokes or Biot subproblems solved in parallel.
result: The interface operator is shown to be positive definite, and convergence of GMRES is analyzed via fields-of-value analysis; numerical experiments demonstrate performance.
conclusion: The proposed method provides a scalable parallel solver for coupled Stokes-Biot systems, with theoretical convergence guarantees.

title: A Polyak-Ruppert Central Limit Theorem For SA-Adam With Momentum And Non-Convergent Adaptive Preconditioning
authors: Xiaoming Huo Sunyoung An
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptive optimizers combining preconditioning, momentum, and weight decay (Adam and AdamW) are, under Polyak-Ruppert averaging, candidate engines for one-pass inference. Does the averaged iterate keep the classical Polyak-Ruppert central limit theorem (CLT), with sandwich covariance [MATH] (Hessian [MATH], gradient covariance [MATH]), under momentum and non-convergent preconditioning? The preconditioner-only analysis does not carry over: with momentum the canonical decomposition collapses to a tautology. Treating the augmented state (iterate, momentum buffer) as a time-varying linear stochastic approximation (SA), we prove (under local stabilization) positive drift stability, a non-autonomous Polyak-Ruppert CLT, and a projection identity. The upshot: the iterate-marginal covariance is exactly the plain stochastic gradient descent (SGD) sandwich [MATH], so the adaptivity is asymptotically invisible. This holds for SA-Adam (sub-linearly vanishing momentum gain, [MATH]; the sub-linear regime is essential), not constant-[MATH] deployed Adam. Coupled [MATH] weight decay yields the ridge-penalized sandwich, extending one-pass inference to regularized problems.
tldr: This paper proves a central limit theorem for the Polyak-Ruppert averaged Adam optimizer with momentum and non-convergent preconditioning, showing the asymptotic covariance matches plain SGD.
motivation: To understand the asymptotic behavior of adaptive optimizers like Adam under Polyak-Ruppert averaging, which are used for one-pass inference.
method: Treats the augmented state (iterate and momentum buffer) as a time-varying linear stochastic approximation and proves positive drift stability and a non-autonomous Polyak-Ruppert CLT.
result: The iterate-marginal covariance equals the plain SGD sandwich covariance, making adaptivity asymptotically invisible; weight decay yields a ridge-penalized sandwich.
conclusion: Under sub-linearly vanishing momentum, SA-Adam's averaged iterate behaves like SGD asymptotically, extending one-pass inference to regularized problems.

title: Inference Optimal Long Run Variance Estimation With Lugsail Kernels
authors: James M. Flegal Rebecca P. Kurtz-Garcia
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17369v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For datasets with unknown but stationary serial dependence, a robust long run variance estimator is essential to handle diverse scenarios. Spectral variance estimators are commonly used but tend to exhibit significant negative bias in the presence of positive correlation. To overcome this, zero lugsail estimators have been introduced, offering zero asymptotic bias regardless of the correlation structure. However, there are currently no guidelines for selecting the optimal bandwidth for lugsail estimators, a critical component in the estimation process. We propose an inference optimal bandwidth rule for lugsail estimators, based on nonstandard fixed-smoothing limiting distributions developed in our study. This approach significantly improves bias correction, accounts for variability, and provides an estimator optimized for robust inference. Our theoretical findings are supported by a simulation study.
tldr: This paper proposes an optimal bandwidth rule for lugsail long-run variance estimators in time series analysis.
motivation: Spectral variance estimators suffer from negative bias under positive correlation; lugsail estimators correct this but lack bandwidth selection guidelines.
method: The authors derive fixed-smoothing limiting distributions for lugsail estimators and propose an inference optimal bandwidth rule based on these distributions.
result: The proposed bandwidth rule improves bias correction and accounts for variability, providing an estimator optimized for robust inference.
conclusion: The new bandwidth rule enhances the performance of lugsail estimators, supported by simulation studies.

title: Coarse Preference Reporting In The Bottleneck Model: Approximate Strategyproofness And Efficiency
authors: Riki Kawase Takara Sakai
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A central operator schedules each vehicle's passage time through a bottleneck to achieve a dynamic system optimum (DSO). The assignment depends on each vehicle's preferred arrival time, which is private and must be elicited from each vehicle. Mechanisms that elicit exact preferences, such as the Vickrey-Clarke-Groves (VCG) mechanism, can achieve strategyproofness but involve relatively complex rules and a computational burden on the operator. We focus instead on coarse reporting, in which each vehicle selects from a finite menu of time slots of a common width. This discrete interface already structures reservation and appointment systems in practice, including managed lanes for automated vehicles, airport slot allocation, and delivery appointment windows. We design a slot-based DSO mechanism on this coarse interface, in which the operator implements DSO assignment based on the reported slots and charges a capacity shadow price as a toll, and evaluate its performance. We prove that both the worst-case misreporting gain and the expected efficiency loss decrease quadratically in the slot width. The efficiency loss decays in this way under binding capacity, while the worst-case misreporting gain requires an additional condition on the preferred arrival time distribution and the schedule cost function. Analyzing the no-toll case, we find that the misreporting incentive persists, however finely the slots are refined, indicating that the toll also serves to elicit truthful reports. Numerical experiments support these theoretical results and show that they continue to hold in parameter regions outside the sufficient conditions.
tldr: This paper studies strategyproofness and efficiency in bottleneck scheduling with coarse preference reporting, using a slot-based mechanism and capacity shadow pricing.
motivation: To design a practical scheduling mechanism that balances truthfulness and efficiency when users report only coarse time slots, reducing complexity compared to exact preference elicitation.
method: The authors propose a slot-based dynamic system optimum mechanism where each vehicle selects from a finite menu of time slots, and the operator assigns passage times and charges a capacity shadow price toll. They analyze worst-case misreporting gain and expected efficiency loss as functions of slot width.
result: Both worst-case misreporting gain and expected efficiency loss decrease quadratically with slot width under certain conditions. Without tolls, misreporting incentives persist even with fine slots.
conclusion: Coarse reporting with appropriate tolls can achieve near-optimal efficiency and truthfulness, making it suitable for practical reservation systems.

title: Convergence Of An Ip Dg Method For The Quad-Curl Problem
authors: Xianhao Zeng
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17428v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work analyzes revises the interior penalty (IP) discontinuous Galerkin (DG) method imposed in [Chen, G., Qiu, W., \& Xu, L. (2021). Analysis of an interior penalty DG method for the quad-curl problem. IMA Journal of Numerical Analysis, 41(4), 2990-3023.] for the quad-curl problem in a nonconvex polyhedral domain, while introducing a piecewise constant coefficient matrix. We derive two main results: Under minimal regularity assumptions, we prove that the numerical solutions converge strongly to the true solution in the [MATH] norm. Under slightly higher regularity, we establish the optimal estimate of the convergence rate depending on the regularity of the solution. These two results, serving as a complement to the existing literature, completely answer how the concerned IP DG method performs on quad-curl problems with low regularity.
tldr: This paper analyzes the convergence of an interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin method for the quad-curl problem in nonconvex polyhedral domains.
motivation: The quad-curl problem arises in electromagnetics and other applications, and numerical methods for nonconvex domains with low regularity are not well understood.
method: The authors revise an existing IP DG method and prove strong convergence under minimal regularity assumptions, and optimal convergence rates under slightly higher regularity.
result: Strong convergence in the energy norm is established, and optimal error estimates are derived depending on solution regularity.
conclusion: The results complement existing literature by fully characterizing the method's performance for quad-curl problems with low regularity.

title: Contextual Robust Optimization For Ai Data Center Scheduling With Statistical Guarantees
authors: Yijie Yang, Xi Weng, Yue Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid growth of AI workloads is substantially increasing data center electricity demand and carbon emissions, motivating the development of carbon-aware scheduling methods. However, effective scheduling is challenging because renewable generation and AI workloads are subject to forecast errors, while training and inference workloads exhibit heterogeneity in computational characteristics. This paper proposes a contextual robust optimization framework for AI data center operation. The proposed model explicitly captures the heterogeneous computational characteristics of AI training and inference workloads. To deal with renewable generation and workload forecast errors, we develop loss-based uncertainty learning models that directly map contextual features to covariate-dependent uncertainty sets. The resulting contextual joint chance-constrained scheduling problem is reformulated into a tractable robust optimization problem, and a calibration algorithm is developed to provide finite-sample probabilistic feasibility guarantees for multiple joint chance constraints. Numerical experiments based on real-world AI workload traces and renewable generation data show that the proposed method reduces operating costs by an average of 5.57% compared to benchmark methods while maintaining reliable feasibility and strong computational scalability.
tldr: This paper proposes a contextual robust optimization framework for carbon-aware scheduling of AI workloads in data centers, with statistical feasibility guarantees.
motivation: The rapid growth of AI workloads increases data center electricity demand and carbon emissions, and scheduling is challenging due to forecast errors in renewable generation and workload heterogeneity.
method: The authors develop loss-based uncertainty learning models to map contextual features to uncertainty sets, reformulate the joint chance-constrained scheduling problem as a tractable robust optimization problem, and design a calibration algorithm for finite-sample probabilistic feasibility guarantees.
result: Numerical experiments using real-world AI workload traces and renewable generation data show an average 5.57% reduction in operating costs compared to benchmarks, while maintaining reliable feasibility and scalability.
conclusion: The proposed framework effectively reduces costs and emissions for AI data center operation under uncertainty.

title: Design Principles For Stable And Generalizable Data-driven Discretizations For Solving Linear Hyperbolic Conservation Laws
authors: Alistair Adcroft Antoine-Alexis Nasser
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate data-driven finite-volume discretizations of the linear advection equation in one dimension. Neural networks for use as numerical advection schemes are constructed adhering to first principles of numerical analysis, allowing us to examine how normalization, training data, and architectural choices influence stability, accuracy, and shape preservation. (i) We show that reconstruction based solely on cell averages leads to a multi-valued learning problem, explaining limited generalization when training data includes widely different curvature regimes. (ii) Numerical stability and good generalization can be achieved by enforcing semilinearity (Lin and Rood 1998) through local stencil-scale normalization, which ensures invariance under affine transformations of the inputs. (iii) A new data-driven flux limiter is introduced that outperforms the classical 'OSTVD3' (Arora and Roe, 1997) scheme in shape preservation by introducing mild antidiffusion in near-linear regimes, while higher-order reconstruction in non-monotonic regions provides limited benefit. (iv) We show that training on polynomial profiles yields stable, high-order accurate discretizations, with the polynomial degree controlling the formal order of accuracy. Together, these results illustrate how the representational, architectural, and training choices govern the stability and generalization of data-driven finite-volume schemes for linear advection.
tldr: This paper studies data-driven finite-volume discretizations for solving linear advection equations, focusing on stability and generalization of neural network-based numerical schemes.
motivation: To design stable and generalizable data-driven numerical methods for hyperbolic conservation laws by incorporating principles from numerical analysis.
method: The authors construct neural network-based advection schemes that enforce semilinearity and local stencil-scale normalization, and introduce a data-driven flux limiter trained on polynomial profiles.
result: They show that reconstruction based solely on cell averages leads to a multi-valued learning problem, and that enforcing semilinearity ensures stability and generalization. The data-driven flux limiter outperforms classical schemes in shape preservation.
conclusion: The representational, architectural, and training choices govern the stability and generalization of data-driven finite-volume schemes for linear advection.

title: An Adaptive Algorithm For The Approximation Of General Linear-Parametric Optimization Problems
authors: Levin Nemesch, Stefan Ruzika, Clemens Thielen, Alina Wittmann
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Linear-multi-parametric optimization problems are a widely studied class of optimization problems. The objective function in such a problem is affine linear dependent on a parameter vector, and the goal is to compute a set of solutions that contains an optimal solution for every fixed parameter vector. However, this is known to be computationally challenging: The underlying non-parametric problem might be NP-hard, and, in addition, optimal solution sets might have exponential cardinality. Parametric approximation aims at providing polynomial-time algorithms that overcome these challenges. Instead of computing an optimal solution set, the goal is to compute an approximation set that contains only an approximate solution for every fixed parameter vector. Several new parametric approximation algorithms have been developed in recent literature. However, all of these share a common set of assumptions, which limits the class of parametric optimization problems that can be approximated. Namely, they do not allow negative parameter dependencies and have their parameter sets fixed to the positive orthant. We present a new adaptive approximation (and, also, exact) algorithm that can be applied to a wider class of linear-multi-parametric optimization problems. Our algorithm builds upon existing algorithms from both the fields of parametric and multi-objective optimization and generalizes these algorithms. In addition, we provide structural results for the transformation of parameter sets, and demonstrate that, for linear-multi-parametric maximization problems, the assumption of non-negative optimal objective values over the whole parameter set is not sufficient to ensure approximability.
tldr: This paper presents an adaptive algorithm for approximating linear-parametric optimization problems, extending existing methods to a wider class of problems.
motivation: Existing parametric approximation algorithms have restrictive assumptions (e.g., no negative parameter dependencies, parameter set fixed to positive orthant). The authors aim to develop a more general algorithm applicable to a broader class of linear-multi-parametric optimization problems.
method: The algorithm builds upon existing parametric and multi-objective optimization algorithms, incorporating adaptive techniques and structural results for transforming parameter sets.
result: The proposed algorithm can handle negative parameter dependencies and arbitrary parameter sets, and it provides both approximation and exact solutions. The paper also shows that for maximization problems, non-negative optimal objective values over the whole parameter set are insufficient to guarantee approximability.
conclusion: The new adaptive algorithm generalizes previous work and expands the class of linear-parametric optimization problems that can be efficiently approximated.

title: Power Mean Transforms Of Operators
authors: Shihai Yang Jing-Bin Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17556v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce the power mean transform [MATH] of an operator [MATH] on a Hilbert space, which is a convex combination of some classical operator transforms such as the mean transform [MATH], the Aluthge transform [MATH], and the Duggal transform [MATH]. In particular, when [MATH] is invertible, this transform coincides with the induced Aluthge transform [MATH] recently defined by Yamazaki with [MATH] for [MATH] and [MATH]. We study basic properties of [MATH] including its spectrum, norm and numerical radius. Moreover, we use the power mean transform to give new characterizations of normal, quasinormal and binormal operators. The questions of Golla et al. and some new results on the Duggal transform are also mentioned. We obtain a result close to the recent one of Osaka and Yamazaki \cite[Theorem 3.3]{yamazaki-tams-2025} on the iteration of the induced Aluthge transform for centered operators. Finally, we describe the form of bijective maps commuting with the power mean transform of the product of matrices.
tldr: This paper introduces a power mean transform of operators on Hilbert spaces and studies its spectral, norm, and numerical radius properties, along with characterizations of normal, quasinormal, and binormal operators.
motivation: To unify and generalize several classical operator transforms (mean, Aluthge, Duggal) via a convex combination based on power means, and to explore their properties.
method: The authors define the power mean transform and analyze its spectrum, norm, and numerical radius using operator theory techniques. They also examine its relation to known transforms and use it to characterize operator classes.
result: New characterizations of normal, quasinormal, and binormal operators are obtained, and connections to the induced Aluthge transform and Duggal transform are established. A result on iteration of the induced Aluthge transform for centered operators is also presented.
conclusion: The power mean transform provides a unifying framework for several operator transforms and yields new insights into operator structure, but the work is purely mathematical with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Weighted Hardy Inequalities Involving Supremum For Decreasing Sequences
authors: Tu\u{g}\c{c}e \"unver, Amiran Gogatishvili, Nurzhan Bokayev, Nurgul Kuzeubayeva
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17558v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we provide a complete characterization of the weighted Hardy inequalities involving the supremum operator, restricted to the cone of non-increasing sequences, for all positive parameters. We reduce such inequalities to equivalent ones on the cone of non-negative sequences. The latter setting provides a broader framework for analysis and significantly expands the range of proofs that can be established.
tldr: This paper characterizes weighted Hardy inequalities involving supremum operators for decreasing sequences.
motivation: To extend classical Hardy inequalities to a more general setting with supremum operators and non-increasing sequences.
method: The authors reduce the inequalities to equivalent ones on the cone of non-negative sequences, enabling a broader analysis framework.
result: Complete characterization of the weighted Hardy inequalities for all positive parameters is provided.
conclusion: The reduction technique expands the range of proofs and provides a unified approach to such inequalities.

title: Two-Echelon Delivery Vehicle Sharing And Repositioning In Hyperconnected Urban Logistic Networks
authors: Benoit Montreuil Xiaoyue Liu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17608v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In response to the growing demand for sustainable and efficient urban deliveries, this study introduces a two-echelon vehicle sharing and repositioning problem for containerized delivery operations within a hyperconnected urban logistics system. We leverage a Physical Internet (PI)-enabled three-tier logistic hub network, comprising gateway, local, and access hubs, to facilitate efficient flows. By adopting containerized delivery, vehicles can rapidly swap standardized modular containers at hubs to reduce handling time. Moreover, inspired by the PI concept of open resource sharing, we determine optimal service routes within a two-echelon structure that jointly utilizes heterogeneous vehicle fleets and enables dynamic vehicle relocation across hubs. We formulate this problem as a multi-period integer program that integrates path-based service vehicle planning with arc-based container routing. To address real-world large-scale instances, we propose a decomposition-based heuristic with capacity-aware flow assignment, which partitions the problem into subproblems structured by echelons and regions. A case study on the Atlanta metropolitan area demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed model and solution approach. Experimental results show that the two-echelon hyperconnected delivery system reduces CO2-eq emissions by 45.0% and total costs by 16.8% at full market share compared to a traditional single-echelon alternative, while enabling vehicle repositioning further lowers costs by up to 17.7%.
tldr: This paper addresses a two-echelon vehicle sharing and repositioning problem in urban logistics using a Physical Internet framework.
motivation: To improve sustainability and efficiency of urban deliveries by enabling vehicle and container sharing across a hub network.
method: Formulates a multi-period integer program and proposes a decomposition-based heuristic with capacity-aware flow assignment.
result: The proposed system reduces CO2 emissions by 45% and total costs by 16.8% compared to traditional single-echelon delivery.
conclusion: Hyperconnected logistics with vehicle repositioning can significantly lower costs and emissions in urban freight.

title: A Projection-Free Algorithm For Variational Inequalities In Hilbert Spaces With Strong Convergence
authors: Reinier Diaz Millan
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17640v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study variational inequalities governed by a point-to-set maximal monotone operator in a real Hilbert space and constrained by a convex inequality \(C=\{x\in\Hi:c(x)\le0\}\), where the defining function \(c\) is continuous and not necessarily differentiable. The proposed method uses only projections onto intersections of half-spaces and avoids the metric projection onto \(C\). Feasibility is handled by subgradient cuts and, when a trial operator point is infeasible, by a Slater correction based on a fixed strictly feasible point. The variational inequality is represented by Minty-type separating half-spaces generated at feasible graph points of the operator, and a Haugazeau half-space is added to obtain best-approximation convergence. Under a Slater-corrected feasible-separation condition, together with explicit exact, approximate and finite-candidate oracle realisations, the whole sequence converges strongly to \(P_{S^*}(x^0)\), the projection of the initial point onto the solution set. We also derive best-iterate \(O(N^{-1/2})\) residual estimates for the step residual, feasibility violation and Minty gap. The analysis is stated directly for point-to-set maximal monotone operators, while the concrete oracle realisations include finite-dimensional single-valued models. We record the consequences of strong monotonicity in the point-to-set setting and provide numerical comparisons on nonsmooth and large-scale constraints, including maxima of convex quadratics, a discretised optimal-control problem, mixed-norm sparse recovery, a Cournot--Nash capacity equilibrium, and a genuine point-to-set \(\ell_1\)-subdifferential example.
tldr: This paper presents a projection-free algorithm for solving variational inequalities in Hilbert spaces with strong convergence guarantees.
motivation: Variational inequalities are fundamental in optimization and equilibrium problems, but standard projection methods can be computationally expensive when the constraint set is complex.
method: The algorithm uses subgradient cuts and Slater corrections to handle feasibility, and incorporates Minty-type separating half-spaces and Haugazeau half-spaces to achieve strong convergence without metric projections onto the constraint set.
result: The whole sequence converges strongly to the projection of the initial point onto the solution set, and best-iterate O(N^{-1/2}) residual estimates are derived for step residual, feasibility violation, and Minty gap.
conclusion: The proposed method is effective for nonsmooth and large-scale constraints, as demonstrated on several numerical examples including a point-to-set ℓ1-subdifferential problem.

title: Robust Bayesian Portfolio Optimization With Discrepancy-based Posterior Ambiguity
authors: Zongxia Liang, Yang Liu, Xingjian Ma
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17643v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a continuous-time robust Bayesian portfolio optimization problem under drift uncertainty of risky assets. The investor learns unknown asset drifts through Bayesian filtering while considering uncertainty around posterior estimates via discrepancy-based ambiguity sets, including Wasserstein and [MATH] distances. To address the resulting time inconsistency, we introduce a feedback-type ambiguity framework that reformulates ambiguity conditionally on observable states. This leads to a modified Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman--Isaacs (HJBI) equation characterizing the value function and the optimal strategy. For a semi-explicit solution example, we use the exponential utility to derive a reduced semilinear parabolic PDE and establish existence of classical solutions via a verification theorem.
tldr: This paper studies a robust Bayesian portfolio optimization problem under drift uncertainty using discrepancy-based ambiguity sets, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: The authors aim to address drift uncertainty in continuous-time portfolio optimization by incorporating ambiguity about posterior estimates.
method: They use Bayesian filtering and discrepancy-based ambiguity sets (Wasserstein and chi-squared distances) within a feedback-type ambiguity framework, leading to a modified HJBI equation.
result: For exponential utility, they derive a semilinear parabolic PDE and establish existence of classical solutions via a verification theorem.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a tractable approach to robust portfolio optimization under model uncertainty.

title: Gray-Box Optimization Using Optimism In The Face Of Uncertainty
authors: Katrin Baumg\"artner, L\'eo Simpson, Moritz Diehl
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17726v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper considers sequential gray-box optimization where the objective function is given as the composition of a loss function and a parametric model. Crucially, the parameters of the model are unknown and need to be iteratively estimated from noisy observations of the model outputs. This problem setup generalizes the parametric black-box optimization problem known as (contextual) stochastic linear bandit. To address the sequential gray-box optimization problem, we propose a structure-exploiting method that leverages known problem structure given in terms of the loss function and an a priori set of admissible parameters. The method is based on the principle of optimism in the face of uncertainty and trades off exploration and exploitation by minimizing a lower confidence bound on the true objective function. We provide a detailed regret analysis of the novel method, improving on state-of-the-art results for the special case of linear stochastic bandits due to the use of a recently published bound for the parameter confidence sets arising in multi-output linear least-squares estimation. Numerical examples illustrate the superior performance of structure-exploiting methods compared to structure-agnostic approaches.
tags: optimism in the face of uncertainty
tldr: This paper proposes a gray-box optimization method using optimism in the face of uncertainty for sequential decision-making with unknown parametric models.
motivation: Many real-world optimization problems involve a known loss function but unknown model parameters, requiring efficient exploration-exploitation trade-offs.
method: The method minimizes a lower confidence bound on the true objective, leveraging known structure (loss function and admissible parameter set) and multi-output linear least-squares confidence sets.
result: A detailed regret analysis is provided, improving on state-of-the-art bounds for linear stochastic bandits, and numerical examples show superior performance over structure-agnostic approaches.
conclusion: Exploiting problem structure in gray-box optimization yields better regret bounds and practical performance compared to black-box methods.
keywords: optimism in the face of uncertainty

title: Sobolev Extensions, Interpolation Inequalities And Consequences
authors: Rupert L. Frank, Pekka Koskela, Riddhi Mishra
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17738v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove Sobolev interpolation inequalities on extension domains that have a form reminiscent of the corresponding whole-space inequalities. This form is crucial in certain applications, which we discuss as well. The technical key ingredient is the notion of a Lebesgue [MATH]-extension domain, which we introduce here, and our proof that, for [MATH], any [MATH]-extension domain is a Lebesgue [MATH]-extension domain.
tldr: The paper proves Sobolev interpolation inequalities on extension domains using a new notion of Lebesgue extension domains.
motivation: To obtain Sobolev inequalities on extension domains that resemble whole-space inequalities, which are crucial for certain applications.
method: Introduces the concept of Lebesgue extension domains and proves that any extension domain is a Lebesgue extension domain.
result: Sobolev interpolation inequalities on extension domains are established in a form analogous to whole-space inequalities.
conclusion: The new inequalities and the notion of Lebesgue extension domains provide useful tools for analysis on extension domains.

title: On The Solution Of Large-scale Non-autonomous Differential Riccati Equations: A Numerical Study
authors: Eugenio Mancinelli, Davide Palitta, Jens Saak
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17744v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We explore the numerical solution of large-scale non-autonomous Differential Riccati Equations (DREs). While we assume to discretize the differential operator using a Backward Differentiation Formula (BDF) of order s, we solve the generalized Algebraic Riccati Equation (gARE) resulting at each time step by different state-of-the-art methods. In particular, we compare the performance of the inexact Newton- Kleinman method with line search and the low-rank RADI iteration, considering for both methods two different initialization strategies: zero initialization and warm-start. A comprehensive panel of numerical results illustrate the potential and limitations of these methods when employed within a numerical pipeline for the solution of DREs, rather than for the isolated solution of a single gARE, as commonly considered in the existing literature.
tldr: This paper studies numerical methods for solving large-scale non-autonomous differential Riccati equations, focusing on comparing the inexact Newton-Kleinman method and the low-rank RADI iteration with different initialization strategies.
motivation: Differential Riccati equations arise in control theory and other applied fields, but their numerical solution for large-scale problems is challenging. The authors aim to evaluate and compare state-of-the-art methods in a time-stepping context rather than in isolation.
method: The differential operator is discretized using a Backward Differentiation Formula (BDF) of order s, leading to a generalized Algebraic Riccati Equation (gARE) at each time step. The gARE is solved by either the inexact Newton-Kleinman method with line search or the low-rank RADI iteration, with zero or warm-start initialization.
result: A comprehensive numerical study shows the performance and limitations of each method when used within a time-stepping pipeline, highlighting trade-offs between accuracy and computational cost.
conclusion: The choice of solver and initialization strategy significantly impacts efficiency; the study provides guidance for practitioners solving large-scale DREs.

title: Optimal Placement And Tuning Of Pointwise Dampers For Vibrating Strings Via A Lyapunov Framework
authors: Ninoslav Truhar Josip Tamba\v{c}a
abstract: ArXiv:2606.17748v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the optimal placement and tuning of a small number of pointwise viscous dampers for a vibrating string. Starting from a finite element discretization of the damped wave equation, the system is transformed into a first-order phase-space formulation, which enables a unified Lyapunov trace framework. Three optimization criteria are considered: average total energy, average total displacement, and energy for a fixed initial state. For all criteria, explicit gradient formulas with respect to damper positions and viscosities are derived, requiring only one primal and one dual Lyapunov solve. Due to the strong non-convexity of the problem, a simple heuristic based on an explicit single-damper formula is proposed to generate effective initial guesses. Numerical examples illustrate the influence of spectral selection and discretization on the optimal damping configuration.
tldr: This paper studies optimal placement and tuning of viscous dampers for vibrating strings using a Lyapunov framework, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To optimize damping in mechanical systems, which is a classical engineering problem.
method: Finite element discretization of the damped wave equation, transformation to first-order phase-space, and Lyapunov trace framework with gradient formulas.
result: Explicit gradient formulas for three optimization criteria and a heuristic for initial guesses.
conclusion: The proposed method effectively optimizes damper placement and tuning despite non-convexity.

title: Time Integration As Filtering: A Space-time Discretization-aware Les Formulation
authors: Syver D{\o}ving Agdestein
